title: Cold-boot amortization and weight residency shepherd for Dedicated fleets
creator: Maya Lin
description: Problem: Cold-start spikes on Dedicated fleets cause transient latency and throughput degradation for SLA customers. Current warm pool heuristics focus on simple LRU residency and bulk prefetching which is expensive and misses tenant-tailored warmups. Goal: amortize cold-boot costs across tenants and time by introducing a lightweight weight residency shepherd and 'cold-boot amortization' admission policy that jointly manages weight residency, KV cache priming, and prewarm admission to meet per-tenant throughput guarantees while minimizing reserved GPU memory and transient load.
acceptance_criteria: Average 95th percentile cold-start latency reduction >= 40% for affected model/tenant combos in controlled canary compared to baseline.
Dedicated fleet node memory overhead from residency metadata < 3% of GPU memory footprint on average.
Automated admission policy respects per-tenant throughput SLA and can be overridden via fleet control API.
End-to-end rollout has documentation, test harness, and a gated feature flag in console and helm charts.
Metrics are visible in Console: per-tenant warm-residency, prewarm admission rate, KV-priming hit rate, and cost delta per hour.
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight residency shepherd process per node that tracks weight residency score computed from recent tenant activity, expected ramp, and on-disk weight locality.
Residency score = alpha * recency_score + beta * tenant_expected_throughput + gamma * prewarm_priority. Tune weights in feature flag.
Admission controller to admit prewarm jobs with budgeted GPU memory and pre-configured time window; supports soft and hard admission policies.
KV cache priming via sampled prefix replays: take 1% production traffic sample (masked for PII) and feed to a sandbox priming pipeline to populate local KV caches before full admission.
Streaming weight loader: stream weight shards in low-priority background IO, accelerate finalization with prioritized shard pinning for imminent requests.
Autoscaler integration point: expose 'residency demand' signal to Dedicated autoscaler so it can proactively scale target capacity when amortized cold-boot debt exceeds threshold.
Cost controls: chargeback accounting by attributing memory residency hours and priming IO to tenant; surfaced in Console billing breakdown.
Fallback behavior: when admission fails or pressure is high, automatically route to compatible lower-capacity variant or smaller-quantized model with monitored quality regression alerts.
